display-pixel.purpose: Lead event headline and auth mark in Silkscreen. Whole-pixel steps only: 96, 64, 48, 32, 24px; 96 steps to 64 below 1180px and 48 below 720px. Uppercase, smoothing off.

display-smooth.purpose: Same slot when the title exceeds 28 characters or contains Arabic. Paired sizes 96→60, 64→44, 48→34, 32→26, 24→20px.

headline.purpose: Page titles and the auth title.

title-sm.purpose: Section titles, rail heading, ticket stub event name, estimate total.

body.purpose: Default text; long prose capped at 52–62ch.

body-lg.purpose: Event descriptions and the lead venue line.

label.purpose: Field labels, table headers, journey cell labels (12px below 720px).

wordmark.purpose: Home link in the top bar, Silkscreen 24px.

status-pixel.purpose: Unresolved status words in blue Silkscreen: 16 / 24 / 32px for sm / md / lg (lg drops to 24 below 720px).

status-smooth.purpose: Settled status words in Schibsted Grotesk 800: 17 / 22 / 30px for sm / md / lg.

ticket-code.purpose: Issued ticket codes on every stub, wrapping anywhere.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The only curve for movement: presses, status sharpen-in, toast entry.

motion.name: color-change
motion.purpose: Background, text and border color changes on buttons, chips, nav links and tier options.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: :active on buttons and chips (stepper buttons scale to 0.94). Disabled controls do not press.

motion.name: dither-out
motion.value: 240ms, stepped repeating-conic-gradient mask (4px then 6px checker) with opacity 1→0
motion.purpose: The settling status's old pixel word breaks up like a print screen.

motion.name: sharpen-in
motion.purpose: The settled smooth status word comes into focus over the dithering pixel word.

motion.name: status-leave-window
motion.purpose: Time the leaving pixel word stays mounted before removal.

motion.name: led-blink
motion.purpose: Next journey cell while the system is working.

motion.name: hover-gate
motion.purpose: All hover effects live behind this query.

motion.name: keyboard
motion.purpose: Keyboard actions (the / search shortcut) never animate.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Dither-out word not rendered, sharpen-in off, blinking off, toast transition off, press scale off.

components.css: .ds-danger-row { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 12px; } .ds-btn-danger, .ds-btn-danger-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-height: 44px; padding: 0 24px; border-radius: 0; font: 600 15px/1.5 var(--font-text, 'Schibsted Grotesk', system-ui, sans-serif); white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 120ms cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1), background-color 120ms ease; } .ds-btn-danger { border: 2px solid var(--danger, #E5011A); background: var(--danger, #E5011A); color: #fff; } .ds-btn-danger-outline { border: 2px solid var(--danger-ink, #B80018); background: transparent; color: var(--danger-ink, #B80018); } .ds-btn-danger:active, .ds-btn-danger-outline:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-danger:focus-visible, .ds-btn-danger-outline:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #2B3BFF); outline-offset: 2px; } @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) { .ds-btn-danger-outline:hover { background: var(--danger-wash, #FCE3E5); } }

components.name: Status Word
components.description: Signature move: live states in blue pixels, settled in smooth ink, failed in red. On settle the pixel word dithers out while the smooth word sharpens in.

components.css: .ds-status-row { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 32px; } .ds-status { white-space: nowrap; } .ds-status-live { color: var(--accent, #2B3BFF); font-family: var(--font-pixel, 'Silkscreen', ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 24px; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1; letter-spacing: 0; text-transform: uppercase; -webkit-font-smoothing: none; } .ds-status-settled, .ds-status-failed { font-family: var(--font-text, 'Schibsted Grotesk', system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 22px; font-weight: 800; line-height: 1; letter-spacing: -0.01em; } .ds-status-settled { color: var(--ink, #0A0A0A); } .ds-status-failed { color: var(--danger-ink, #B80018); } .ds-status-out { animation: ds-dither-out 240ms forwards; color: var(--accent, #2B3BFF); } .ds-status-in { animation: ds-sharpen-in 200ms cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1) 140ms both; } @keyframes ds-dither-out { 0% { opacity: 1; } 33% { -webkit-mask: repeating-conic-gradient(#000 0 25%, transparent 0 50%) 0 0 / 4px 4px; mask: repeating-conic-gradient(#000 0 25%, transparent 0 50%) 0 0 / 4px 4px; } 66% { -webkit-mask: repeating-conic-gradient(#000 0 12.5%, transparent 0 50%) 0 0 / 6px 6px; mask: repeating-conic-gradient(#000 0 12.5%, transparent 0 50%) 0 0 / 6px 6px; } 100% { opacity: 0; } } @keyframes ds-sharpen-in { from { opacity: 0; filter: blur(3px); } to { opacity: 1; filter: blur(0); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-status-out { display: none; } .ds-status-in { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
The app is a printer's proof of a distributed system. Anything still unresolved (a booking waiting on the saga, a live state, a code the system issued) is set in a coarse bitmap face; anything settled is set in a fine grotesk. When a booking state resolves, its status word visibly breaks up and sharpens into smooth type, so the asynchronous backend is something you watch rather than something hidden behind an instant "done".

The material is newsprint: a warm paper ground, true black ink, 2px ink rules dividing every region, square corners, no shadows and no gradient fills. One synthetic electric blue carries actions and live state; signal red appears only when something failed or is about to be destroyed. Imagery is never photography: every event and ticket gets a halftone plate of square dots generated from its id. Density is high and list-like (a sortable table of what's on, a rail of bookings), with the lead event set like a flyer in large pixel type.

Motion is short, stepped and print-like. Presses compress, the live journey cell blinks like an LED, and the one expressive transition is the status settle: dither out, sharpen in. Everything that moves stops for reduced-motion users, and nothing animates in response to a keyboard shortcut.
keyCharacteristics: Pixel type (Silkscreen) for unresolved and identity text, smooth type (Schibsted Grotesk) for everything people read or type.
Status resolution, pixel to smooth, as the signature move on every booking and ticket state.
One accent (#2B3BFF) for actions and live state; red only for failure and destruction.
2px ink rules, square corners, flat surfaces; depth comes from rules and the paper / paper-raised step.
Generated halftone squares, seeded by id, as the only image material.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Electric blue (#2B3BFF) marks only what you can act on and what is in flight. It is never a heading color, a decoration, or a category tint.

rules.name: The Red Means Broken Rule
rules.body: Signal red fills (#E5011A) and red text (#B80018) appear only for failure and destructive actions. Never for prices, urgency, emphasis or "hot" events.

rules.name: The Whole-Pixel Rule
rules.body: Silkscreen is set only at whole multiples of 8px: 16, 24, 32, 48, 64 or 96px. Responsive changes step between these values; nothing scales the pixel face fluidly or lands between steps.

rules.name: The Unresolved-In-Pixels Rule
rules.body: The pixel face is reserved for the wordmark, display titles (event headlines, empty-state titles, the auth mark), status words in a waiting or live state, and ticket codes. Everything people read or type is Schibsted Grotesk.

rules.name: The Fallback Rule
rules.body: A title longer than 28 characters, or containing Arabic (U+0600–06FF, U+0750–077F, U+FB50–FDFF, U+FE70–FEFC), renders in Schibsted Grotesk 800 at the paired smooth size, with dir="auto" for Arabic. The pixel face has no Arabic glyphs and stops reading well past that length.

rules.name: The No-Tnum Rule
rules.body: Never enable tabular figures (tabular-nums / tnum) on text: this face widens commas, colons and full stops under tnum. Numeric columns align right instead.

rules.name: The Flat Proof Rule
rules.body: No shadows, no gradients, no surface blur. If a surface needs separation, give it a 2px ink rule or the paper-raised ground.

rules.name: The Dither Exception
rules.body: Hard-stop repeating-conic-gradient checkers are 1-bit dither patterns, not gradients: they are allowed as the loading-row texture and the status dither-out mask. The 3px blur is allowed only inside the sharpen-in transition.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Radius is always 0. A rounded corner anywhere is a bug.

rules.name: The Halftone-Only Rule
rules.body: The only image material is the generated halftone: square dots on a grid (24 × 16 cells by default), density from three soft blobs placed by a generator seeded with the event or ticket id, so each item keeps the same plate forever. Dots are capped below the cell size so the screen never closes into a solid. Ink dots on Proof White; inverted to paper dots on ink in the auth art.

dos: Do set unresolved and machine-issued text (live status words, ticket codes) in Silkscreen, and switch it to Schibsted Grotesk 800 once it settles.
Do keep Silkscreen at 16, 24, 32, 48, 64 or 96px only, weight 400, uppercase, letter-spacing 0, smoothing off.
Do fall back to Schibsted Grotesk 800 at the paired smooth size for titles over 28 characters or containing Arabic.
Do align numeric columns right instead of using tabular figures.
Do divide regions with 2px ink rules and lift content surfaces to Proof White (#FBFAF7) on Newsprint (#F2F0EB).
Do give every event and ticket a halftone plate of square dots seeded by its id.
Do use the ease-out curve cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1), 120ms press at scale 0.97, and gate hover behind (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine).
Do remove movement and blinking under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
donts: Don't use the pixel face for body copy, form text, buttons, nav links, or at any size that is not a whole multiple of 8px.
Don't turn on tabular-nums or tnum on text; the face widens commas, colons and full stops.
Don't use Electric Proof Blue (#2B3BFF) for anything other than actions and live state.
Don't use red (#E5011A fills, #B80018 text) for anything other than failure and destructive actions.
Don't add shadows, gradient fills or rounded corners.
Don't use photography, stock imagery or round halftone dots; plates are generated square dots only.
Don't animate in response to keyboard actions, or fake an instant success: a state that is still in flight stays in pixels until the backend settles it.
